title: backlog part 2: pbi.* behind its own retry-constant lock, byte-exact docs/backlog.md render + --check, mixed-runtime race proof
action: Split out of rpl-6 on review, which was the largest cell in the batch (11 verbs, two lock protocols, two row schemas, a byte-exact renderer, a git side effect and a concurrency contract — five independent deliverables). This cell carries the second half: pbi.add, pbi.status, pbi.amend, pbi.list, render, and render --check. Handlers in packages/bee/bee.mjs:3670-4007; lib in packages/bee/lib/backlog.mjs. THREE exact-replication requirements. (1) THE SECOND LOCK. addPbi takes a module-local lock via acquireStoreLockOnceSync with its OWN retry constants — packages/bee/lib/backlog.mjs:106-108 (REVIEW-CORRECTED anchor; :91-105 is the rationale comment) BACKLOG_PBI_LOCK_RETRY_ATTEMPTS=15 and delay 20ms, with MAX_PBI_ID_GEN_ATTEMPTS at :114. Do NOT consolidate it onto withDecisionsLockSync: the retry counts differ and D3/D9 freeze observable protocol semantics. File the duplication as a follow-up PBI via `bee backlog propose` instead. Port BacklogPbiLockBusyError (backlog.mjs:120) and the bounded collision-retry id generator (backlog.mjs:87, crypto.randomBytes(4)) with its exact error contract. (2) LOCK CONFORMANCE, which output diffing cannot see. Add a race test in the shape of crates/bee-core/tests/decisions_lock_conformance.rs where a live mjs writer and the Rust binary run pbi.add concurrently against the same .bee/backlog.jsonl — assert zero lost rows, no interleaved partial lines, and that the busy-error contract fires identically from both runtimes once the retry budget is exhausted. (3) THE RENDERER. docs/backlog.md is rendered from an event-sourced fold over TWO coexisting row schemas — legacy friction/finding rows and kind:pbi rows — and `render --check` refuses if stale. Byte-exact markdown table formatting, ordering, blank lines and trailing newline; semantic equality is not acceptance. REVIEW-FOUND FIXTURE GAP: crates/queen-bench/src/fixture.rs:296 emits every backlog row as type `proposal`, so NEITHER schema the fold branches on is present in the baseline store, and no docs/backlog.md exists at all. Seed both schemas per-scenario using the seeding rpl-1 provides. Register --cmd-check scenarios: pbi.add/status/amend/list round-trip; pbi id collision forcing the retry loop; render into a repo with both row schemas seeded; re-render for idempotence; --check against a hand-drifted file with the verdict AND message compared.

truths: cargo test -p bee-core --test backlog_lock_conformance passes, with the mixed mjs/rust concurrent pbi.add case reporting zero lost rows over at least 50 rounds and an identical busy-error contract from both runtimes
cargo run --release --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p bee-parity -- --cmd-check --group backlog reports every part-2 scenario clean, docs/backlog.md byte-identical between runtimes
the render scenarios seed BOTH row schemas rather than reading the monotone all-proposal baseline store
render is idempotent — a second run leaves the file byte-unchanged — and --check reports the same verdict and the same message as mjs on a drifted file
the pbi id collision retry loop and BacklogPbiLockBusyError contract match mjs exactly, including the attempt counts
a follow-up PBI is filed for consolidating the two lock implementations after mjs retires

the workspace test run at the head of this cell verify is green with --no-fail-fast, so no cross-cutting pin has rotted outside every cell own gate (the rpl-3 goal-check found one that had been false for two cells because it sat outside every verify and was never executed)
